quote: Let Xi ~ M(theta_i), i = 1, 2 be two random variables. If theta_1 <= theta_2, then X1 <lr X2, X1 <hr X2, X1 <s X2 and X1 <cx X2
family: Mgamma distribution M(theta): pdf f(x) = theta^3 x (1 + x/2) e^{-theta x} / (1+theta), x > 0, theta > 0; a finite mixture of Gamma(2, theta) and Gamma(3, theta) with mixing probability theta/(1+theta)

hypotheses.text: Let Xi ~ M(theta_i), i = 1, 2 be two random variables.
Likelihood Ratio order (X <lr Y), if f_X(t)/f_Y(t) is decreasing in t.
hypotheses.formal: X <=lr Y iff f_X(t)/f_Y(t) is nonincreasing in t

quantifiers: theta_1, theta_2 > 0 with theta_1 <= theta_2; all t > 0
ambiguity: The proof computes d/dt[f_X1(t)/f_X2(t)] = -(theta_1 - theta_2) e^{-(theta_1 - theta_2)t} < 0, 'forall theta_1 >= theta_2', which contradicts the stated hypothesis theta_1 <= theta_2: the ratio decreases in t (giving X1 <=lr X2) only when theta_1 >= theta_2. As printed, the hypothesis and the inequality direction in the proof disagree. The 'X <lr'/'X <s' symbols are written with the prec glyph in the PDF.

Convex order (X <cx Y) if for all convex functions phi and provided expectation exist, E[phi(X)] <= E[phi(Y)].

hypotheses.text: if E[X] = E[Y], then Convex order <=> Stochastic order.

quantifiers: theta_1, theta_2 > 0 with theta_1 <= theta_2; all convex phi
ambiguity: The cx conclusion relies on Remark 2's equivalence 'Convex order <=> Stochastic order if E[X] = E[Y]', but E[X] = (2theta+3)/(theta(1+theta)) is strictly decreasing in theta, so E[X1] != E[X2] whenever theta_1 != theta_2; the stated sufficient condition for cx does not hold. Inherits the hypothesis-direction conflict of the lr part.
